instructions: Complete the summary below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
stem_block:
What was thrown out, and why

Cereals, and rice above all, made up the largest slice of the edible waste, with vegetables not far behind, while the biggest inedible category by some way was (37) ........ from fruit and vegetables, above all from bananas and mangoes. Drinks added a little more: modest quantities of coffee and tea went down the sink, usually because more had been brewed than anyone meant to finish. Asked to account for their losses, families in the two districts said much the same things — food going mouldy, a change in the feel of meat or fish, and bread that keeps for too short a time. Dairy items, meanwhile, were regularly overlooked at the back of the (38) ........ and only thrown out once it was too late. Country households still wasted far less, since leftovers there were more often turned into compost or given to animals; town households leaned instead towards (39) ........ and bought more than they required. For the authors, the lesson is that policy has so far dealt with collecting and disposing of waste; real (40) ........ , they argue, will depend on campaigns that name the particular foods concerned.

items.explanation: Paragraph E says that among inedible waste, fruit and vegetable peelings, led by banana and mango skins, made up the largest share; so the answer is 'peelings'.

items.prompt: Town households leaned instead towards (39) ........ and bought more than they required.
items.evidence: Urban residents, by contrast, tended to favour convenience and were more prone to buying more than they needed, a pattern the researchers connect to busier schedules and greater purchasing power rather than carelessness.
items.explanation: Paragraph H says that city dwellers favoured convenience and were more likely to buy more than they needed; so the answer is 'convenience'.

items.prompt: For the authors, the lesson is that policy has so far dealt with collecting and disposing of waste; real (40) ........ , they argue, will depend on campaigns that name the particular foods concerned.
items.evidence: The authors argue that food waste policy in Indonesia, as in many countries, has focused on collection and disposal rather than prevention, and that meaningful reductions will depend on tackling the specific items and behaviours identified in the study, rather than treating food waste as a single undifferentiated problem.
items.explanation: Paragraph I says that food waste policy has focused on collection and disposal rather than prevention, and that meaningful reductions depend on tackling the specific items identified in the study; so the answer is 'prevention'.
